resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR, Forest Lookouts and the county inventory give 100 feet (30.5 m) for the tower. A 1967 survey note (quoted on the Forest Lookouts page and in the inventory) gives an overall height of 90 feet. The record keeps 100 feet, the height most sources give; the story notes the 90-foot figure.

NHLR names MnDOT as administrator. The county inventory's owner column reads Mn MFS (Minnesota Forest Service, now the DNR Forestry Division), which is probably the original owner. No source gives a transfer date, so both are reported.

notes_for_editor: Access is the main gap. The fence is from a 2004 recovery note and the 'not opened' status rests on an NHLR line of unknown date; no current source. visit.climbable is null because no source says either way, and access.level is unknown because the fence is dated 2004; treat the access block as unverified until MnDOT or DNR confirms. Search results surfaced an undated travel guide that says a tower can be seen from the road; not used. The inventory notes 'Rainy Lake lookout' as an alternate name, not added to the record's other_names. No new photos.
